content: Cephradine is a cephalosporin antibiotic that is prescribed to treat bacterial infections, including pneumonia, as well as infections of the ear, skin, throat, and urinary tract. It is not effective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other conditions; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Cephradine is available in capsule form or as a liquid to be taken orally. It is typically taken either every six hours (four times daily) or every twelve hours (twice daily) for a duration of 7 to 10 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. Continue taking cephradine for the full prescribed duration, even if you feel better. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before starting cephradine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to cephradine, other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cefadroxil or cephalexin), penicillin, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), probenecid, or vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, colitis, or stomach problems. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking cephradine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking cephradine. Take cephradine at least one hour before or two hours after meals. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Cephradine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, and mild skin rash. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention and include severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, unusual bleeding or bruising, sore throat, painful mouth or throat sores, and vaginal infections. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store cephradine capsules in their original container, tightly closed, at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Discard any expired or unused medication. Liquid cephradine should be stored in the refrigerator, tightly closed, and discarded after 14 days. Do not freeze the liquid. It can also be stored at room temperature for up to 7 days. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and any required laboratory tests. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to cephradine. If you have diabetes, consult your doctor before making any changes to your diet or medication dosage. Use Clinistix or TesTape to test your urine for sugar while taking cephradine, as Clinitest is not recommended. Do not share this medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of cephradine, contact your doctor. Cephradine is sold under the brand name Velosef®.
